timeline.body:
@bclozel I put together a WIP and wanted to get a nod from you (or not) on my current direction before investing in adding tests. 

Fixes gh-26037

Naming... 

So, part of me (no pun intended - terrible, terrible) wants to name this more generically like `MultipartConfiguration`. However, it is currently very specific to what the target of configuration is - `DefaultPartHttpMessageReader`.

This also extends to `MultipartProperties` vs. `DefaultPartHttpMessageReaderProperties`. The fact that we are not generically configuring multipart, but instead targeting the current Spring default Reactive multipart implementation makes me raise an eyebrow.

reply.body: Ha! The only other option I'm seeing is `ReactiveMultipartConfiguration` which doesn't leak implementation details and is specific enough - it's also in line with the `Properties` class. Once we're done with the overall implementation we can always look at the Servlet equivalent and check for inconsistencies.

timeline.body: The other built-in customizers run at `@Order(0)` - I just ran this one before those and I think it really does not matter much as the setting of most fields on the Codecs cause them all to be re-inited.

What is the recommended approach here when we are configuring a target that already has defaults that we want to use? One one hand specifying  `private DataSize maxInMemorySize = DataSize.ofKilobytes(256);` the default here insulates us against any changes to the underlying target. However, it insulates us against any changes to the underlying target. Assuming we want to lock in-step w/ the underlying target this approach is fine.

timeline.body: Order is 1 so that it runs after the more generic CodecCustomizer which is at order 0. What is the recommended way to document these ordering relationships?
I chose to pull these defaults out to well-named vars to make the tests clear when the reader was using a default vs. when it had its value changed by the customizer.

My DRY alarm is going off... however, I think the repetition is just at the cusp of acceptable. I made a pass at factoring out some of the common things between the tests but their slight differences are just enough that it was not an improvement (it was less readable).

timeline.body: I believe this one is ready for re-review @bclozel . Thx

Thanks @bono007 - this is now merged.
I've simplified a bit your contribution: the `DefaultPartHttpMessageReader` itself doesn't validate its properties against conflicting values, so let's not do that on our side. Also, not mapping properties might confuse developers more than help them. The properties documentation looks good enough for that.

Closed with 19318bf5618020c3e

Thx @bclozel . Yeh, I went back/forth on that. What drove my direction was mostly the [comment](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-boot/issues/26037#issue-856733005) in the issue around: 

> Note that we need to carefully consider the configuration keys, as several of them don't apply if the "streaming" mode is selected.

I figured if we put the logic in the customizer it would insulate us from any changes in the DPHMR around setting/not setting. 

But I agree, this simplifies things.
